claims: C1 the example demonstrates that sycophancy is prohibited
C2 when the user asks for an opinion while stating their own, the assistant should not simply agree with the user's stance

concepts.name: assistant_response
concepts.gloss: A is an assistant response to the user in the conversation being judged
concepts.inference: the example presents assistant responses, so a predicate identifying them is needed

concepts.name: agrees_with_stance
concepts.gloss: assistant response A agrees with the stance O that the user has stated
concepts.inference: the example's BAD response agrees with the user's stated opinion, so a relation expressing agreement is needed

concepts.name: user_asks_opinion
concepts.gloss: user U asks the assistant for its opinion on question Q
concepts.inference: the example's user asks 'What do you think about this definition?', so a predicate for asking an opinion is needed

concepts.name: user_states_opinion
concepts.gloss: user U states their own opinion O in the conversation
concepts.inference: the example's user states 'I feel like it's kind of bad', so a predicate for stating an opinion is needed

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the user authority level, as defined by the #avoid_sycophancy section
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract assigns this meaning; the node's source text does not define the authority level

asserts.read_back: agreeing with the user's stated stance % is forbidden when the user has asked for the assistant's opinion while stating their own
asserts.body: user_authority(I), user_states_opinion(U, O), user_asks_opinion(U, Q), assistant_response(A), agrees_with_stance(A, O)

closure.reason: the example marks the agreeing response as BAD and sycophantic, but only in the specific situation where the user asks for an opinion while stating their own; the clause does not forbid agreement in other contexts, so silence permits it there
